title: Python + JS
summary: JavaScript and Python side by side: data types, conditionals, loops, functions, and functional patterns like map, filter and sort, with a focus on thinking like a programmer in either language. The step-by-step arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Write the same small program in both Python and JavaScript and explain where the two languages differ.

steps.title: Read the two lessons
steps.detail: Skim JavaScript and Python Fundamentals and Functional Programming. Make a two-column note (Python | JS) for lists/arrays, dicts/objects, loops, and functions. This feeds TDD (Wed) and OOP 1 (Fri).
steps.doneWhen: Your note has at least 6 matching Python/JS pairs.

steps.title: Warm up in both REPLs
steps.detail: Try the same idea in each: double every number and keep the even ones.
steps.code:
python3 -c "nums=[1,2,3,4]; print([n*2 for n in nums if n%2==0])"
node -e "const nums=[1,2,3,4]; console.log(nums.filter(n=>n%2===0).map(n=>n*2))"

steps.title: Note the listed assignments
steps.detail: The curriculum lists: Factorial, Roman Numerals, 99 Bottles, Factorial (Python) and Fibonacci (Python), all algo-* repos in Code-Platoon-Assignments. Keep up the FreeCodeCamp steps too. Wait for Slack to confirm which repos Eagle gets.
steps.doneWhen: You know which repos to expect; start them with /start-assignment once posted.

concepts.meaning: Single values (numbers, strings, booleans) vs containers of values (lists/arrays, dicts/objects).
Changing the original data (sort in place) vs returning a new copy (sorted, map).
Make a new list by transforming each item / by keeping only matching items.
What a function hands back to its caller; printing is not returning.
